Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
5 layers fold at the '=' cell: position-addressed hard attention reads op+bit, a 3-ReLU gate updates state S; no LayerNorm, attention is a transient read.
One tied block iterated 10 times as a causal cellular automaton: rotated-position attention reads cell p-1, 3-ReLU gate recomputes state; op tokens carry their neutral bit.
Depth lower-bound check: same tied CA with one iteration too few (T=9), so state cannot reach the '=' cell from the last bit.
Tied CA with the minimal gate: S_new = relu(k-A) - relu(2k-3+X-A), two ReLU neurons compute AND/OR/XOR on k=S+b.
Tied skip CA: head 0 reads state+op from p-2, head 1 reads the bit at p-1, so state hops odd cells and 5 iterations suffice (half the depth of the 1-head CA). Buggy: state was read through head 1.
Fixed skip CA: head 0 carries op flags AND state from p-2 (W_v is independent of q/k dims), head 1 reads the bit at p-1; 5 iterations.
Tied CA keeping real LayerNorm: dual-rail encoding fixes every cell's mean and variance, so LN is a constant scale cancelled by its gain; 2-neuron gate; no head bias.
Tied CA with parameter cuts: closed-form sinusoidal position buffer, no W_o (W_v routes state onto the bit channel), centred state so the head has no bias.
Tied CA with attention wholly in a 2-D position plane (2x2 W_q/W_k); logic space is just 4 channels (A,X,b,S).
Tied CA with a scalar state: tokens embed to (A,X,b), the MLP outputs only S, and the head reads only S.
Scalar-state CA without W_k: keys are raw positions and W_q is a scaled rotation, sharpness beta=200.
Noise-margin sweep: same CA with softer attention, beta=20 (neighbouring cell leak about e^-2.7).
Noise-margin sweep: same CA with beta=8 (neighbouring cell leak about e^-1.07, roughly 34% relative weight).
Aliasing test: position circle with theta=pi/3 wraps every 6 cells, so p-1 and p-7 tie in the attention scores.
Tightest non-aliasing position circle: theta=2pi/11 gives each of the 11 sequence cells one slot.
CA with content addressing instead of a position circle: each cell attends to the most recent token of the opposite kind (bits read ops, ops read bits), using only a scalar position and a type flag.
No MLP and no ReLU: the gate is a 9-row (op, S+b) truth table read by nearest-neighbour attention; softmax is the only nonlinearity.
Non-iterative 3-layer circuit: classify instructions, count prefix flips with a dominated softmax (true sum), jump to the last reset and take parity of value + flips after it.
Ablation: dominated softmax weakened to L=2, so the flip count is no longer a true sum (denominator depends on position).

Ablation: triangle wave cut to 4 neurons; predicted to fail on exactly one prompt (y=5, 1^1^1^1^1=). NOT actually perfect: exhaustive check is 2591/2592; the 200-sample eval missed the failing prompt.
Robustness probe: full constant-depth circuit with Gaussian noise (sigma=0.02, fixed seed) added to every parameter.

Robustness probe: opposite-kind CA with Gaussian noise at the same sigma=0.02 (fixed seed, different draw because parameter shapes differ) added to every parameter; iterations now equal sequence length.
Opposite-kind CA with a 2-neuron signal-restoration clamp after the gate (flat logic levels), under sigma=0.02 weight noise (one fixed-seed draw, not the same vector as the unrestored run).
Restoring CA stress test: Gaussian weight noise raised to sigma=0.1 (fixed seed).
Restoring CA noise bisection: Gaussian weight noise sigma=0.05 (fixed seed).
Noise-free restoring CA, also checked exhaustively on all 93312 unseen 7-bit expressions with the same weights (iterations = sequence length).
Restoring CA with very soft attention (beta=0.6, next opposite-kind cell at about 30% relative weight): does restoration also absorb attention leak?
Recommended model: tied causal CA; attention has a fixed query and two gains (attend to most recent opposite-kind token), a 2-neuron AND/OR/XOR gate, a 2-neuron restoring clamp; length-agnostic.
